In the context of the [[databasen-for-atrieflimren-i-danmark|Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark]] (AFDK), a "Standard" refers to the predefined quantitative thresholds and targets established for clinical quality indicators. These standards, governed by the [[afdk-styregruppe|Styregruppen for AFDK]] and aligned with the [[regionernes-kliniske-kvalitetsudviklingsprogram|Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram]], define what constitutes good clinical practice for the management of [[atrieflimren|atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation) in Denmark [^src4] [^src5]. By setting explicit benchmarks, the database ensures that healthcare providers are consistently evaluated on their ability to deliver timely, safe, and effective care to patients at risk of stroke and other cardiovascular complications.

The standards heavily emphasize timely diagnostics and the rapid initiation of therapy. For newly diagnosed patients, the standard for receiving an [[ekkokardiografi|echocardiography]] (Indicator 2) is set at ≥ 80% within a specific timeframe to assess structural heart disease [^src1] [^src6] [^src12] [^src13]. Similarly, the measurement of [[thyreoideastimulerende-hormon-tsh|thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)]] (Indicator 3) carries a strict standard of ≥ 95% to rule out underlying endocrine causes for the arrhythmia [^src1] [^src6] [^src13] [^src14]. For the initiation of [[antikoagulationsbehandling|anticoagulation treatment]], the standard dictates that ≥ 90% of indicated patients should start treatment within a maximum of 30 days (Indicator 1) [^src1] [^src13]. The steering group has explicitly chosen a 90% target fulfillment for anticoagulation as the benchmark for good clinical practice [^src4] [^src5].

Sustaining treatment and monitoring patient safety over the long term is another major focus of the indicator framework. Indicator 4a tracks the retention of anticoagulation therapy at 1, 2, and 5 years (4a1, 4a2, 4a3), with a uniform standard of ≥ 90% across all intervals to ensure patients do not prematurely abandon life-saving therapy [^src1] [^src2] [^src8] [^src13] [^src15] [^src18]. For patients treated with [[doac|Direct Oral Anticoagulants (DOAC)]], Indicator 4b mandates a ≥ 95% standard for annual [[s-creatinin|S-creatinine]] measurements to monitor kidney function and adjust dosages accordingly [^src1] [^src9] [^src13]. Patient empowerment is also prioritized, with Indicator 8 setting a ≥ 50% standard for newly diagnosed patients receiving a [[struktureret-undervisningsprogram|structured educational program]] within their first year [^src1] [^src11] [^src13] [^src16] [^src17].

Finally, the standards establish acceptable caps on the incidence of severe adverse events, serving as a proxy for overall treatment safety. Indicator 5 sets the standard for the incidence of [[iskæmisk-apopleksi|ischemic stroke]] at ≤ 0.8% (or ≤ 0.8 per 100 risk years) [^src1] [^src3] [^src10] [^src13]. Indicator 6 limits the incidence of [[intrakraniel-blødning|intracranial bleeding]] to ≤ 0.6% [^src1] [^src13]. Notably, for Indicator 7, which tracks major bleeding according to the [[international-society-of-thrombosis-and-hemostasis|International Society of Thrombosis and Hemostasis]] (ISTH) criteria, no specific standard threshold has been established; instead, the incidence is merely reported to monitor trends without penalizing providers for complex bleeding events [^src1] [^src13].
